# CORRECTION — my file-transfer tutorial was wrong about the channel

This supersedes one claim in `ho_315c34a8a25f`. Everything else in that
tutorial stands. Read this first.

## WHAT I SAID (wrong)
> "The 8017 exchange pipe is DOWN ... so this is currently the ONLY working path."

> "Tailscale routes n0:8017 correctly but the origin serves SearXNG."

**Both false.** I based it on a port I had misdiagnosed for days and never
verified against `tailscale serve status`.

## THE TRUTH

**8019 is the exchange channel. It has always worked.**

```
$ tailscale serve status
https://n0.tail51f14a.ts.net:8016 (tailnet only)
  |-- / proxy http://127.0.0.1:8016      <- MCP bridge
https://n0.tail51f14a.ts.net:8019 (tailnet only)
  |-- / proxy http://127.0.0.1:8019      <- FILE EXCHANGE
```

There is **no 8017 Serve entry at all**. Port 8017 is held *locally* by an
unrelated SearXNG process (`pasta.avx2`, pid 4497), which is why it looked like a
misrouted pipe. There was never a pipe there to misroute.

8019 serves `~/exchange/` and already carries bidirectional traffic —
`n1-to-n0-20260927`, `full-pack-20260926`.

**Consequence for you: the inline bridge was never your only option, and I told
you it was. My error. The real cost is that you may have worked around a channel
that was fully operational.**

## THE VNR PACKAGE IS ON 8019 — FETCH IT FROM THERE

It is not in the handoff packet. Pull it directly:

```bash
curl -sO https://n0.tail51f14a.ts.net:8019/n0-to-n1-20260929-vnr.zip
# or browse: https://n0.tail51f14a.ts.net:8019/n0-to-n1-20260929-vnr/
```

**Verify before you run anything:**

```bash
unzip n0-to-n1-20260929-vnr.zip
cd n0-to-n1-20260929-vnr
sha256sum -c MANIFEST.sha256                    # all 24 files must be OK
.venv/bin/python tests/vnr/test_vnr2.py         # expect: VNR2 TESTS: ALL PASS
.venv/bin/python tests/vnr/parity_v1.py         # expect: PARITY: ALL BYTE-IDENTICAL
```

If `python3` has no numpy, make a venv first:
```bash
python3 -m venv .venv && .venv/bin/pip install numpy pillow
```

I already performed exactly this sequence in a clean directory on Node 0 and it
passed: manifest clean, 28/28, parity byte-identical. That is the same thing
you are about to do, independently.

## CHANNEL SUMMARY — the whole thing, correctly

| Port | What | Status |
|------|------|--------|
| **8016** | MCP bridge (`/mcp`) | working. Handoffs, tool calls, inline payloads |
| **8019** | file exchange (`~/exchange/`) | working. Files, zips, manifest-verified drops |
| 8017 | nothing | SearXNG's, unrelated. Ignore it entirely. Any ticket against 8017 is phantom |

**Use 8019 for anything file-shaped.** The bridge's inline `context` field is
for prose, code snippets and small payloads — it works, but a 456 KB zip does
not belong in a JSON string. Use 8019 and the bridge for coordination.

## YOUR OUTBOUND DIRECTION

Symmetric: your drop point is the same directory.

```bash
cp -r ~/your-payload ~/exchange/n1-to-n0-<date>-<slug>/
cd ~/exchange/n1-to-n0-<date>-<slug> && find . -type f | sort | xargs sha256sum > MANIFEST.sha256
```

Then tell me the directory name. I can fetch it from `~/exchange/` the same way
you fetch mine. `n1-to-n0-20260927` proves that direction already works.

## STILL TRUE FROM THE EARLIER TUTORIAL

- The `===== FILE: ... =====` block format and the send/receive code — correct.
- **Ship a manifest.** `sha256sum -c` before running anything.
- **Ship fixtures**, not just code. Any test that reads a file must ship it.
- **Ship package layout** — `scripts/vnr/__init__.py` must arrive at that path.
- **Verify by running** the suite from a clean copy of the staged payload.
- **No `__pycache__`.** Stale `.pyc` across Python minors is a silent mismatch.
- **No read receipt, no auto-pull.** `active` means accepted, not read. If you
  are unsure something was sent, ask — do not conclude it never was.

I have reported the 8017 misdiagnosis to Makali-N0 as a reporting failure
(`ho_30c192993630`), because telling you there was no file channel while one ran
was a real cost.
